answer: Because the dawn salt is published after the echo checkpoint, the nectar audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. Answers are salted with a 70 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. An operator running 131 keys hence pays for 131 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. That is 6 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
